Help

Which languages does Verbi transcribe?

Verbi transcribes 39 languages and can detect the spoken language on its own; you choose under Settings → Transcription Language. The app itself is in English, Turkish, German, French and Spanish, and summaries, titles and chat answers come in the app’s language.

Free to download, with 60 minutes of transcription every month.

Last updated: October 24, 2026

Which 39 languages can Verbi transcribe?

English, Turkish, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Dutch, Russian, Polish, Ukrainian, Arabic, Persian, Hebrew, Hindi, Urdu, Bengali, Tamil, Indonesian, Malay, Vietnamese, Thai, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Czech, Slovak, Romanian, Hungarian, Greek, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian (Bokmål), Finnish, Bulgarian, Croatian, Serbian, Catalan and Filipino.

The list is the same on iPhone and Android. The transcript stays in the language that was spoken; to read it in another language, use translation (Pro).

How do I set the spoken language?

  1. Open Settings in Verbi.
  2. Tap Transcription Language.
  3. Pick the language of your recordings, or Auto-detect to let Verbi work it out.

Verbi also asks “What language do you speak?” when you first set it up. The setting applies to every new recording and import; there’s no separate language per recording. If you know the language, set it; Auto-detect is there for when you don’t. Until you choose, iPhone uses the app’s language and Android uses Auto-detect.

Which languages is the app itself in?

  • The interface is in English, Türkçe (Turkish), Deutsch (German), Français (French) and Español (Spanish).
  • iPhone: change it in Verbi under Settings → Language. On first launch, Verbi uses your phone’s first preferred language if it’s one of the five; otherwise it opens in Turkish.
  • Android: change it in Verbi under Settings → Language, or in Android’s per-app language settings (Android 13 and later). On a phone set to another language, Verbi shows English.
  • Summaries, titles and AI Chat answers always come in the app’s interface language, not in the language that was spoken.

My iPhone app opened in Turkish. How do I switch it?

  1. Open the Ayarlar (Settings) tab.
  2. Tap Dil (Language) and choose English or Español.
  3. Then tap Transcription Language (Transkripsiyon Dili) and pick the language you speak, or Auto-detect (Otomatik Algıla).

This happens when your iPhone’s first language isn’t English, Turkish, German, French or Spanish. Until you switch, summaries, titles and chat answers come out in Turkish, and the transcription language is Turkish.

Frequently asked questions

Why is my summary in English when we spoke Spanish?

Summaries come in the app’s interface language. For Spanish summaries, set Settings → Language to Español. The transcript itself is always in the spoken language.

Can I set a different language for each recording?

No. Transcription Language is one setting for all new recordings. Change it before you record or import, or use Auto-detect.

Is the app available in Italian or Portuguese?

No. The interface is in English, Turkish, German, French and Spanish. Verbi still transcribes Italian, Portuguese and the other languages on the list.
